subject: Staggered cutover & exception intake — Nimbus migration coordination
messages:
From: Jane Smith <jane.smith@nimbus.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T15:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: staggered cutover exception for Nimbus migration

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the heads-up on the API/model deprecation scheduled July 15. We just ran the pre-cutover load test and are seeing a 3x amplification on a small subset of our batch scoring traffic when routed to the new model family. The SLO hit is transient but could affect our downstream latency SLAs for a handful of enterprise customers.

Concrete ask: can Redwood grant a temporary staggered cutover exception for our account for 6 weeks (through Aug 26) while we validate the inference path and apply the recommended quantized weights? If an exception is possible, wed like a short list of operational constraints (routing policy, tokenization differences to watch, and any recommended rate limits).

I attached a short SLO report and a sample export from our batch jobs for your reference. Happy to hop on a call — Rajesh (cc'd) is our infra lead and can join.

Thanks,
Jane
Director, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: Nimbus_slo_report.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Smith <jane.smith@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: staggered cutover exception for Nimbus migration

Jane — thanks for the clear write-up and the SLO PDF. We can absolutely triage this. Im looping in Marissa for the commercial/contract side and Ben/Naomi to scope the operational exception.

Quick asks from our side before we propose an exception window:
- Can you confirm the top 3 customer IDs affected and typical qps per second for the batch jobs?
- Is the amplification reproducible with the attached nimbus-usage-export.csv (if you can send one)?
- Any existing rate-limit rules (ingress) we should be aware of?

Operationally we have two common approaches: a short-lived routing shim to keep the legacy model serving for flagged customer IDs, or a temporary increased capacity reservation on Dedicated for peak windows. Id like Ben to weigh in on effort and migration risk.

Ive tentatively scheduled a 30-min sync (invite pending) for Wednesday; if that works for you we can lock scope and run a live repro in the call.

—Karthik
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nimbus-usage-export.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: staggered cutover exception for Nimbus migration

Folks — forwarding Nimbus's ask. Short summary and proposed internal asks: 

Summary:
- Nimbus requests a 6-week exception to the July 15 model cutover due to a 3x latency amplification in a subset of batch scoring.
- External provided an SLO report and a sample export; they will join the Wednesday sync.

What I need from product/infra (Ben/Naomi):
1) Risks/effort estimate for a routing shim keyed by customer IDs (approx complexity: low/med/high). If low, we might offer that as an operational stop-gap.
2) If shim is non-starter, estimate for a Dedicated capacity burst and how that impacts cost and SLA.
3) Any known tokenization/decoder differences between model v2.1 and v3 that could explain amplification (product).

Operational constraints to propose back to Nimbus if we grant an exception:
- Exception window: prefer 4 weeks with an optional 4-week extension (we can negotiate).
- Limited to flagged customer IDs; no account-wide exception unless contract amendment.
- Increased tracing and debug logs enabled for the flagged flows; Redwood will bill for any added observability baseline.

Please reply with quick bullets only (Im trying to keep Nimbus waiting time low). If you want to talk live, Ben has 11–11:30 today.

> 
> Thanks for the heads-up on the API/model deprecation scheduled July 15...

—Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Smith <jane.smith@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: staggered cutover exception for Nimbus migration — exception intake confirmed

Hi Jane / Rajesh — thanks for the data and for jumping on the call earlier. Internal summary: product + infra have proposed a pragmatic two-step plan we can offer as an exception.

What Redwood is offering (conditional exception):
1) Exception window: 4 weeks (Jul 15  Aug 12) with a one-time 4-week extension on mutual agreement.
2) Scope: limited to the three customer IDs you identified in the call (please confirm in reply).
3) Mechanism: routing shim for flagged IDs plus temporary Dedicated capacity reservation for peak batch windows.
4) Requirements from Nimbus: enable debug tracing for the affected flows for the duration, provide an updated usage export weekly, and accept potential surcharge for Dedicated usage during peak windows.

Next steps / deliverables:
- I will send an intake exception form and a short mutual action plan for signatures (attached once countersigned).
- Karthik/Bob (Ben) to provide a short runbook for the shim and an ops playbook by EOD tomorrow.
- Finance will surface surcharge estimate; expect a separate note from Naomi.

If that all sounds correct, reply here confirming the three customer IDs and your agreement to the debug tracing requirement. Once we have that well send the exception package for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: exception-form-signed.pdf, mutual-action-plan.docx
